pinned.bed_finish: Toasted Oak frame, Twill Sand headboard

excluded.miles_dresser_60: owner: about 57 in is the maximum on the west wall
excluded.owned cube_organiser: owner: the cube storage goes in every new layout (Today still shows it as the baseline)

required.storage: compare storage with today's nine cube-organiser cubes (assumed 11 x 11 x 11 in each); for dressers without a published drawer volume use an estimate of 0.55 x the case volume above the legs, labelled 'estimate'; less storage than today is a warning, not invalid
required.nightstands: two preferred; one allowed with a warning; existing pieces allowed

main_route.note: measured with doors in their everyday state; below 20 is invalid; 24 tight, 30 comfortable, 36 generous are rules of thumb; IRC R311.6 36-in hallway is a reference only

bed_side_strip.note: width of the strip beside each long side of the bed, measured on its own (the destination, not a route through it); 18 tight, 24 comfortable

drawer_standing.report: standing space in front of a fully open drawer, one drawer at a time

passage.body_model: routes use floor-level obstacles (anything from the floor to 24 in high) plus anything above 24 in that projects more than 3 in from the wall; window stools and casings projecting 3 in or less do not narrow routes (people pass them), but still count for furniture collisions
passage.doors: white door and closet door: at least 90 degrees (a piece may be the stop); entry door: fully open to the south wall. Report each resting angle.

everyday_state.shaker_door: closed (owner: often closed; leads to the primary bathroom)

doors.rules: white door and closet door must be able to open to at least 90 degrees (a piece may be the stop); entry door fully open to the south wall
doors.report: main walkway with doors in their everyday state (decides the class); separately, the narrowest point with the white door open at its stop and with the closet door open, each with the difference from Today; below 20 in with a door open is a warning, not invalid, unless the brief marks that door as usually open
doors.preference: more opening is better for the bathroom door; at least 90 degrees required; about 105 is acceptable to the owner; report the open-door gap at the bed foot as a trade-off

ranking: filter invalid; cluster (bed wall, route pattern, furniture mix); pick distinct representatives; then sort lexicographically by BANDS, not raw inches: (1) main walkway band: 30+ comfortable, 24-30 tight, 20-24 minimal; (2) windows: no headboard or piece taller than 40 in in front of window glass, each window comfortable to open (glass hidden by pieces above the stool, as % of each window, smaller is better; a headboard over glass counts double); (3) bed-side band: both sides 24+, 18-24, 15-18; (4) style fit per brief.style; (5) two nightstands (owned or new) over one; (6) storage band versus Today: at least as much, within 25% less, more than 25% less; (7) real catalog product over generic size; (8) fewer changes; (9) lower cost. Within equal bands, prefer the larger raw walkway. Show Today plus four distinct valid or conditional layouts first, then up to eight; pinned layouts always shown. Each card states in plain words why it ranks where it does when a window or nightstand factor decided it.

style.direction: Angela: mid-century modern; warm walnut or oak, tapered legs, simple lines; should sit well with the Miles bed in Toasted Oak
style.catalog_tags: each catalog piece gets style_fit (strong / partial / weak, with a one-line reason from its materials, finish and form) and tier (budget / mid / premium); record the basis
style.ranking: insert after the bed-side band: (style) strong before partial before weak; budget-tier pieces are recommended only when no mid or premium piece reaches the same bands, and are labelled 'budget option'

placement_sanity: storage pieces stand with their back against a wall (gap = baseboard, or the stool or casing standoff where a window requires it) unless the brief explicitly allows floating; the wall label comes from the back face's contact; drawer fronts face open floor; a piece is never left a few inches off a wall without a named reason; summaries name what changes concretely (e.g. 'queen where the king is, Paris dresser on the west wall') instead of 'with furniture moved'
plain_policy: Keep a queen Miles bed reachable from both sides; nothing may collide or stop a door short; the main walkway from the hall door past the foot of the bed must stay at least 20 inches; bed sides at least 15 inches (today's north side is about 16.75); everything else is a trade-off measured against today. Priorities in order: main walkway, bed-side room, storage, fewest changes, cost.
bed_orientations: head south only if no door swing behind it (closet wall)

windows.model: 3D. Judge each piece in front of a window by its height and depth, not by the width it covers. Window coverage by width is no longer a warning.
windows.operable: an adult standing at the piece's front can open the sash if the horizontal reach from the piece's front edge to the glass plane is at most 24 in (comfortable) or 30 in (limit) and the piece's top is at most 40 in high. Single-hung windows: unlock at the meeting rail, lift the lower sash. Past the limit the window counts as not openable: a warning, and invalid only if it leaves the bedroom with no openable egress-candidate window.
windows.glass_hidden: report the percentage of glass area hidden (piece height above the visible glass bottom x overlapping width, over the glass area) as a preference; pieces at or below the stool top hide none
windows.stool_and_casing: a piece may slide under a stool only if its top is below the stool's underside (stool top minus 1 in); otherwise it stands off the wall by the stool projection (the casing depth beside the opening); a headboard over a casing or stool is a warning
windows.headboard: a headboard whose top is above the stool may overlap the window casing (warning: 'headboard covers X in of the window trim'), but overlapping the window opening (glass) is a strong ranking penalty: 'headboard covers X% of the east window'. Beds may still sit under a window if the headboard is below the stool or the bed has none, which the catalog does not offer yet.
windows.per_piece_reach: report reach only for the piece that stands between the best operating spot and the sash; do not list pieces that are beside a window but not in the way (no 'front-to-glass 86 in' for a bed's length)

child_safety: none: the household has no children (Daniel, 16 Nov 2026). Note manufacturer anti-tip kits for tall pieces as ordinary advice only.

classes.invalid: collision, a door short of its required angle, main route below 20 in, a bed side below 15 in, or a required item missing, at the best estimate
classes.conditional: passes at the best estimate but fails in a plausible joint scenario; name the measurement that settles it
classes.preference: warnings and trade-offs, each stated as a difference from Today

calibration.rule: Today (the arrangement the household lives in) must classify as valid. Any rule that Today fails is a preference comparison ('tighter than today by X in'), not invalid. Enforce with a test.
calibration.today_reference: report every measure for Today and show each layout's difference from Today

wall_items_policy: switches and keypads reachable over pieces up to 24 in deep (warning otherwise); a covered receptacle is a warning
movables: the rolling laundry sorter is movable: it may touch trim and casings and its position is approximate; place it where it does not block a route, door or switch

plain_text.layout_sentence: one sentence of at most 25 words per layout, in plain words, saying what changes and its main trade-off (e.g. 'Queen where the king is, keep the cube shelves: same 27-inch walkway, 7 more inches on the north side, covers a sliver of the east window.')
plain_text.verdict: at most three short sentences at the top: what ranks first and why; how the requested dresser layouts do (door closed and door open); the one measurement that matters most
plain_text.details: keep the full long description per layout (all measures with +/- and differences from Today) in an expandable section and the tables; the short summary sentence comes first

dresser_length_tradeoff.note: parent estimate, thin-leaf model, dresser 2 in off the north wall; stop range = camera-fit hinge 62.15 to survey 62.9
dresser_length_tradeoff.rule_of_thumb: each inch shorter adds about 2.5-3 degrees of door opening between 56 and 40 in; below about 34 in the door folds nearly flat; gaps assume the bed 2 in off the east wall (add 1.25 if flush)

envelopes: for every wall run and window, compute and show the largest piece that passes each rule: maximum depth, height and length, with +/- (e.g. 'Under the north window: up to 24 in deep and 40 in tall keeps it easy to open; up to 27 in tall hides no glass'; 'West wall: up to 56.9 in long; each inch of depth costs an inch of walkway'). One short table per wall on the page, computed by the engine.
parametric_sweep: besides catalog pieces, evaluate generic storage at depths 14, 16, 18 and 20 in, lengths in 2-in steps from 30 in to the span, heights 30-36 in (dresser) and 44-54 in (chest), on every wall run including under windows. Show the depth and length trade-offs, and name the catalog pieces nearest the best generic sizes. Label generic pieces 'generic size, no product chosen'.
rotation: every piece may take any quarter turn where its front stays usable (drawer fronts face open floor; a nightstand's drawer faces the bed or the room); beds take all four headings and may float off walls; low pieces may sit under windows. Prune, but report how many arrangements were evaluated.
generic_sizes: generic sizes show what size works; in the gallery, replace a generic piece with the nearest real catalog product within 2 in of length and 1 in of depth if one exists (including PROJECT/products/shallow-storage-2026-11-16), and say which; keep a generic piece only when no product fits, labelled 'generic size, no product chosen', at most two in the gallery
consistency: every wall named in text (e.g. 'chest west') must be computed from the placed footprint's geometry after rotation; add a test that compares each text label with the footprint's nearest wall and that rotated footprints are the same in plan, 3D, window checks and layouts.json
envelopes_sanity: each envelope value must be physically possible for that wall run (depth at most the room dimension minus the opposite clearance, length at most the run); show 'not limiting' instead of meaningless values such as a 118-in depth or a 2-in length; one row per rule a person would care about: deepest, tallest, longest, each with what limits it
